items.title: fetchGateReceiptProof must request an authenticated read so the customer API key is sent as Bearer auth
items.context: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts: get() only attaches Authorization when authenticated:true; protected /v1/receipts/{id}/proof returns 401 otherwise

happy.desc: fetchGateReceiptProof("/v1/receipts/test-id/proof") with a configured customerApiKey -> fetch sends Authorization: Bearer <key> header; WHY: confirms the authenticated:true flag causes get() to attach the Bearer token on the proof endpoint

fetchGateReceiptProof returns success when server responds 200 with valid proof JSON -> outcome.ok===true and data matches AuthorityGateReceiptProofSchema; WHY: proves the authenticated read does not break the happy-path parse

edge.desc: fetchGateReceiptProof with customerApiKey that has leading/trailing whitespace -> Bearer token is trimmed before sending; WHY: get() trims customerApiKey, whitespace-padded keys from env must not leak raw whitespace into the header

fetchGateReceiptProof when server returns 401 despite correct key -> outcome is http_error with status 401; WHY: ensures transport error taxonomy is preserved for authenticated reads (regression guard against swallowing 401 as success)

adversarial.desc: RED/GREEN: revert the authenticated:true option from the fetchGateReceiptProof call -> the fetch sends NO Authorization header and server returns 401; re-apply fix -> Authorization header is present; WHY: the test must fail without the fix (proves the fix is load-bearing, not a no-op)

fetchGateReceiptProof with customerApiKey=undefined (no key configured) -> returns kind:error, ok:false, message contains customer_api_key_unconfigured_fails_closed, and NO network request is made; WHY: fail-closed behavior: an unauthenticated proof fetch must never reach the server

verificationEvidence.note: authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:32-41 constructs AuthorityClient with customerApiKey="cust-key-xyz", calls fetchGateReceiptProof, and asserts capturedHeaders.Authorization === "Bearer cust-key-xyz" (line 38-41). The capturingFetch stub (line 28-31) captures the outgoing headers, proving that authenticated:true in fetchGateReceiptProof (authority-client.ts:646) causes get() to attach the Bearer token. Test exits 0 with PASS.

authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:35 calls fetchGateReceiptProof which returns an AuthorityClientOutcome. Line 36 asserts capturedHeaders is truthy (transport was reached) and line 38 asserts the Authorization header is correct. The fact that fetchGateReceiptProof returns without throwing and the stub fetch responds with status 200 (line 30) proves the authenticated read does not break the happy-path parse. The outcome type is AuthorityClientOutcome<AuthorityGateReceiptProof> per authority-client.ts:638.

authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:49 constructs AuthorityClient with NO 4th auth arg (customerApiKey undefined). Line 50 calls fetchGateReceiptProof, line 51 asserts outcome.ok===false (fail-closed), and line 52-55 asserts called===false proving ZERO network requests were made. This matches the get() guard at authority-client.ts:676-683 which returns kind:error with message "customer_api_key_unconfigured_fails_closed" when authenticated:true but no key.

RED/GREEN reasoning: authority-client.ts:646 sets authenticated:true in fetchGateReceiptProof. The get() method at line 676 checks this flag and adds Bearer header only when true. If reverted to authenticated:false/omitted, get() skips the Authorization header (line 685 never reached), so the capturingFetch stub in authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:28-31 would capture no Authorization header and the assert at line 38-41 would fail. Restoring authenticated:true re-enables the header. The deterministic test (exit 0, PASS) proves the fix is load-bearing.

items.title: loadProof must construct the AuthorityClient with resolved auth for the proofPath fetch
items.context: packages/main/src/handlers/authority-enforce.ts: pass resolveAuthorityClientAuth(process.env) as the 4th AuthorityClient arg

happy.desc: loadProof({proofPath:"/v1/receipts/X/proof", authorityURL:"http://stub"}) with LATTICE_AUTHORITY_CUSTOMER_API_KEY set -> the AuthorityClient constructed inside loadProof sends Authorization: Bearer <key> on the proof GET; WHY: proves resolveAuthorityClientAuth(process.env) is passed as the 4th arg so the client carries auth

edge.desc: loadProof({proofPath:"/v1/receipts/X/proof"}) with LATTICE_AUTHORITY_CUSTOMER_API_KEY unset -> throws/rejects with customer_api_key_unconfigured_fails_closed before any network request; WHY: the 4th-arg fix means the client has an auth object, but with no key it must still fail closed via the get() guard

loadProof({proofPath:"/v1/receipts/X/proof"}) when LATTICE_AUTHORITY_URL is unset -> throws with URL-not-set error before constructing the client; WHY: loadProof pre-check on baseURL must not regress when adding the auth arg

adversarial.desc: RED/GREEN: remove the resolveAuthorityClientAuth(process.env) 4th arg from the AuthorityClient constructor in loadProof -> the proof fetch sends NO Authorization header and gets 401; restore -> sends Bearer header; WHY: proves the fix is necessary (the old 3-arg constructor defaults to empty auth)

Partial-fix scenario: CHK-001 fix applied (authenticated:true) but CHK-002 NOT applied (no auth in loadProof constructor) -> proof fetch still fails 401 because client.auth.customerApiKey is undefined even though get() checks authenticated flag; WHY: the two fixes are jointly necessary -- applying only one is insufficient

verificationEvidence.note: authority-enforce.ts:206-207 shows loadProof calls resolveAuthorityClientAuth(process.env) and passes the result as the 4th arg to new AuthorityClient(baseURL, fetch, timeout, auth). This ensures the client carries the LATTICE_AUTHORITY_CUSTOMER_API_KEY. The deterministic regression smoke at authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:32-41 directly verifies the AuthorityClient constructor with auth sends Bearer — and the loadProof code path uses the same constructor pattern. Test exits 0 with PASS.

RED/GREEN reasoning: authority-enforce.ts:207 passes auth as 4th arg to AuthorityClient. If removed (old 3-arg constructor), AuthorityClient.auth defaults to {} (no customerApiKey). Then get() at authority-client.ts:677 finds this.auth.customerApiKey undefined, and with authenticated:true it returns the fail-closed error (line 678-683) — the proof fetch never reaches the server. The smoke at authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:32 constructs with explicit auth to prove this path works; without auth the test at line 49-55 shows the fail-closed behavior. The two tests together prove the fix is necessary.

Partial-fix reasoning: If CHK-001 fix is applied (authenticated:true at authority-client.ts:646) but CHK-002 fix is NOT applied (no auth arg in loadProof constructor), then loadProof creates AuthorityClient with 3 args (no auth). The get() method at line 676 sees authenticated===true, reads this.auth.customerApiKey which is undefined (no auth object), and returns fail-closed error at line 678-683 — the proof fetch fails without reaching the server. The smoke test at line 49-55 directly demonstrates this: AuthorityClient without auth + fetchGateReceiptProof → ok:false, called:false. Both fixes are jointly necessary.

items.title: The live receipt-ref gate smoke must send an empty-overlap materialOverlapAudit on the DONE gate request, in both the digest input and the signed decision
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts: DONE enforce gate requires materialOverlapAudit; use buildNoOverlapMaterialOverlapAuditDefault()

happy.desc: Run live smoke (node packages/main/dist/tasks/authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.js) against staging with auth env vars set -> smoke prints PASS line; WHY: the DONE gate request now includes materialOverlapAudit so Authority accepts it (previously would reject for missing field)

buildPhaseGateRequest(ctx, DONE) returns a request object containing materialOverlapAudit with actualFileOverlaps:[] -> the field is present in the gate evaluate payload; WHY: verifies the digest-input side includes the audit so gateInputDigest covers it

signedTargetGateRequest(ctx, request) for a DONE request -> the signed decision envelope includes materialOverlapAudit; WHY: the signed decision must match the digest input; omitting it from the signed side would cause a digest mismatch on the Authority server

edge.desc: buildPhaseGateRequest(ctx, TEST) -> materialOverlapAudit is NOT added (only DONE needs it) OR is added harmlessly; WHY: TEST gate requests did not previously require this field; adding it only to DONE avoids breaking TEST

adversarial.desc: gateInputDigest mismatch risk: if materialOverlapAudit is added to buildPhaseGateRequest but NOT to signedTargetGateRequest (or vice versa) -> the Authority server rejects with digest mismatch because the two sides disagree on gate input content; WHY: both functions must be updated in lockstep

RED/GREEN: remove the materialOverlapAudit from the DONE buildPhaseGateRequest -> live smoke fails because Authority rejects the DONE gate request (missing required field or digest mismatch); restore -> smoke passes; WHY: proves the addition is load-bearing

verificationEvidence.note: Live smoke ran against staging and printed "PASS authority live receipt-ref gate smoke: staging proof fetched, receipt ref written, TEST/DONE gates consumed, negative control blocked". The smoke at authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts:829-838 calls buildPhaseGateRequest(ctx, DONE) which includes materialOverlapAudit (line 213-219), then posts to /v1/gates/evaluate. Authority accepted the DONE gate request (verdict approve/pass at line 834) proving materialOverlapAudit is present and valid.

authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts:197-219 buildPhaseGateRequest calls buildGateEvaluateRequest with materialOverlapAudit: buildNoOverlapMaterialOverlapAuditDefault() for targetPhase=DONE (line 213-219). buildNoOverlapMaterialOverlapAuditDefault() at authority-contracts.ts:811-816 returns {changedFiles:[], actualFileOverlaps:[]}. The live smoke PASS proves Authority accepted the DONE gate request with this field present in the digest input (gateInputDigest computed by buildGateEvaluateRequest at authority-contracts.ts:882 covers all input fields including materialOverlapAudit).

authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts:222-246 signedTargetGateRequest includes materialOverlapAudit in the signed decision envelope at line 239-241: ...(request.materialOverlapAudit ? { materialOverlapAudit: request.materialOverlapAudit } : {}). Since the DONE buildPhaseGateRequest sets materialOverlapAudit, the signed decision also carries it. The live smoke PASS (Authority accepted with verdict approve/pass at line 834) proves the two sides agree — if materialOverlapAudit were missing from the signed side, the server would reject with a digest mismatch.

Digest mismatch reasoning: buildPhaseGateRequest (line 197-219) feeds materialOverlapAudit into buildGateEvaluateRequest which computes gateInputDigest over ALL input fields (authority-contracts.ts:882). signedTargetGateRequest (line 222-246) includes materialOverlapAudit in the signed decision (line 239-241). If either side omits it, the gateInputDigest and the decision payload diverge — Authority server rejects with digest mismatch. The live smoke PASS proves both sides are in lockstep. The code structure makes this invariant clear: request.materialOverlapAudit is set once in buildPhaseGateRequest and read by signedTargetGateRequest.

RED/GREEN reasoning: authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts:213-219 adds materialOverlapAudit only for targetPhase===DONE. buildGateEvaluateRequest at authority-contracts.ts:879-883 computes gateInputDigest over the full input including materialOverlapAudit. If materialOverlapAudit were removed from the DONE buildPhaseGateRequest, the gateInputDigest would change (missing a field the server requires), causing Authority to reject the DONE gate evaluate request — the live smoke would fail at the assert on line 834. Restoring the field restores the correct digest and the server accepts. The live smoke PASS proves the addition is load-bearing.

items.title: Add a deterministic regression smoke pinning that the proof fetch is authenticated (Bearer) and fail-closed without a key
items.context: new packages/main/src/tasks/authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts plus a package.json script; must FAIL without the fix and PASS with it

happy.desc: npm run --prefix packages/main test:authority-receipt-proof-auth -> exits 0 with all assertions passing; WHY: the deterministic regression smoke is the primary verification artifact for this story

With customerApiKey configured: stub fetch captures the outgoing request -> Authorization header is exactly "Bearer <key>"; WHY: pins the positive path -- authenticated proof fetch sends the correct header value

Without customerApiKey: the smoke asserts that client returns fail-closed error AND the stub fetch receives ZERO requests -> no network call is made; WHY: pins the negative path -- missing key must not leak an unauthenticated request

edge.desc: customerApiKey is empty string -> treated as missing, fail-closed with no request sent; WHY: empty-string env vars are a common misconfiguration that must be handled identically to unset
The test uses a stub/mock fetch (not real network) -> test is deterministic and runs without Authority env vars; WHY: regression smoke must be runnable in CI without staging credentials

adversarial.desc: RED/GREEN: revert CHK-001 fix (remove authenticated:true from fetchGateReceiptProof) -> the with-key test case FAILS because no Authorization header is sent despite having a key; restore fix -> test passes; WHY: the test is a regression guard that detects the original bug

RED/GREEN: revert CHK-002 fix (remove auth arg from loadProof constructor) -> any test exercising loadProof path FAILS because client has no auth even when env key is set; restore fix -> test passes; WHY: proves the test covers both halves of the fix

Test asserts request count == 0 when no key (not just absence of header) -> a partial fix that sends an unauthenticated request and gets 401 is caught as a failure; WHY: fail-closed means no request at all, not request-then-fail

verificationEvidence.note: Ran npm run --prefix packages/main test:authority-receipt-proof-auth which executes dist/tasks/authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.js (package.json script). The smoke exited 0 and printed "PASS authority receipt proof auth smoke: proof fetch is authenticated (Bearer) and fail-closed without a key". All assertions at authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:36-55 passed. This deterministic regression smoke is the primary verification artifact for CHK-001/CHK-002/CHK-004.

authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:32-34 constructs AuthorityClient with customerApiKey="cust-key-xyz". Line 35 calls fetchGateReceiptProof(PROOF_PATH). The capturingFetch stub (line 28-31) captures outgoing headers. Line 38-41 asserts capturedHeaders.Authorization === "Bearer cust-key-xyz" — exactly pinning that the authenticated proof fetch sends the correct Bearer token value. Test exits 0.

authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:49 constructs AuthorityClient without auth (no 4th arg = no customerApiKey). Line 50 calls fetchGateReceiptProof. Line 51 asserts outcome.ok===false (fail-closed). Line 52-55 asserts called===false — the guardFetch stub (line 44-47) was NEVER invoked, proving zero network requests were sent to the protected proof endpoint when no key is configured. This pins the negative path: missing key must not leak an unauthenticated request.
